edges.description: Disease alleles change ZASP binding to protein kinase C (D626N, increased) and to phosphoglucomutase 1 (exon 4 and 10 alleles, reduced).
Cells transfected with mutant ZASP show cytoskeletal disarray. The steps between the variant and the disarray are not defined.
In a transgenic mouse, cardiac expression of S196L ZASP altered L-type calcium and sodium currents. ZASP complexes with both channels.
Heterozygous LDB3 variants are associated with noncompaction, but no study describes how they disturb ventricular compaction.

Rare LDB3 variants are reported in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy probands. How a Z-disc variant would produce hypertrophy is not described. Whether LDB3 causes hypertrophic cardiomyopathy at all is disputed (see the CMH24 subtype and discussions).

Proposed link: changed PKC binding by the LIM domains could disturb PKC signalling. The only in vivo support is that mice lacking the LIM-containing long isoforms show PKC pathway changes. That is a deletion model, not a missense allele.
Both binding studies propose that the binding change contributes to dilated cardiomyopathy. Neither tests it in the heart.

edges.description: In Cypher-deficient mouse hearts, the Z-line defect comes with changed ERK, Stat3, calcineurin-NFAT, PKC and actin-MRTFA-SRF signalling.

edges.description: The S196L model study proposes that altered channel complexes explain conduction defects and arrhythmia in LDB3 cardiomyopathy. No human electrophysiological study tests this.

nodes.description: Disease alleles change which partners ZASP holds at the Z-disc. D626N in the third LIM domain increases binding to protein kinase C. The exon 4 alleles S189L and T206I, and I345M in exon 10, reduce binding to phosphoglucomutase 1 (PGM1). Under stress, ZASP normally anchors PGM1 at the Z-disc. All of this comes from binding assays and cultured cardiomyocytes, not from patient tissue.

nodes.description: Cardiac deletion, in development or in adult myocardium, causes severe dilated cardiomyopathy with ultrastructural disruption and death before 23 weeks. ERK and Stat3 activity is increased.

Human electrophysiological data for this mechanism are lacking.

nodes.description: A heterozygous germline missense variant in LDB3 alters ZASP/Cypher, a Z-disc scaffold that binds alpha-actinin through its PDZ domain and protein kinase C through its C-terminal LIM domains. Reported alleles cluster in the cardiac-preferred exons 4 and 10 (S196L/S189L, T213I/T206I, I352M/I345M) or in the third LIM domain (D626N). Whether these act by gain of function, dominant interference or partial loss is unresolved, so the functional impact is recorded as UNKNOWN. Heterozygous loss-of-function carriers in the recessive families were reported as asymptomatic, which argues against simple haploinsufficiency.

These are all deletion models. Whether a heterozygous missense allele engages the same pathways in the human heart has not been tested, so the node is HYPOTHETICAL for CMD1C.

nodes.description: ZASP is not needed to build the Z-disc but keeps it intact during contraction, acting as a linker-strut. Mutant ZASP disarranges the cytoskeleton of transfected cells. Loss of Cypher in mice fragments and disorganizes Z-lines in heart and skeletal muscle. No patient myocardium with a dominant CMD1C allele has been examined at this level in the cited sources.
